Encrypt a payload as a JWE

Source: R/jwe.R
jose_encrypt.Rd

jose_encrypt() encrypts plaintext to one recipient, or to several through jose_recipient(), and returns the JWE in the compact, flattened JSON or general JSON serialization (RFC 7516).

Usage

jose_encrypt(
  plaintext,
  key,
  alg = NULL,
  enc = "A128CBC-HS256",
  header = NULL,
  unprotected = NULL,
  aad = NULL,
  format = c("compact", "flattened", "general")
)

Arguments

plaintext

The plaintext: a raw vector, or a single string taken as UTF-8 text.

key

A jose_key, or a list of jose_recipient() objects for several recipients.

alg

The key management algorithm, such as "A256KW" or "dir". NULL takes the key's own alg.

enc

The content encryption algorithm. "A128CBC-HS256" is the one RFC 7518 requires every implementation to support.

header

Further protected header members, as a named list.

unprotected

Shared unprotected header members, as a named list. Only the JSON serializations carry them.

aad

Additional authenticated data, as a raw vector or a string. Only the JSON serializations carry it.

format

"compact", "flattened" or "general". Several recipients need "general".

Value

The JWE, as a single string.

Details

Encryption generates a fresh content encryption key and initialization vector for every message, so it needs cryptographic randomness from zucrypt (>= 0.2.0). Until that is installed it raises zujwt_unsupported_error; decryption works without it.

See also

jose_decrypt().

Examples

key <- jose_key_oct(as.raw(1:16), kid = "kek")
# Until zucrypt (>= 0.2.0) supplies randomness, this is unsupported.
try(jose_encrypt("secret", key, alg = "A128KW"))
#> Error in jose_encrypt("secret", key, alg = "A128KW") : 
#>   Encryption needs random keys and IVs from zucrypt (>= 0.2.0).
